title: HRW 12e Conceptual Practice Quiz — LaTeX Math Variant

questions.question: What does Lenz's law state about the direction of an induced current?
choices: (a) It enhances the change in flux
(b) It is independent of flux changes
(d) It opposes the change in flux that produced it
questions.answer: (d) It opposes the change in flux that produced it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law says the induced current creates a magnetic effect that opposes the change in magnetic flux (consistent with energy conservation).

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: According to Faraday's law, the magnitude of the induced emf in a loop is proportional to:
choices: (c) The rate of change of magnetic flux
questions.answer: (c) The rate of change of magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Faraday's law is $\lvert\mathcal{E}\rvert = \left|\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt}\right|$, so only how fast the flux changes matters.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: Which expression correctly defines magnetic flux through a flat loop area $A$ in field $B$ at angle $\theta$?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is $\Phi_B = \vec B\cdot\vec A = BA\cos\theta$.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: In motional emf, charges in a conductor moving with velocity $\vec v$ through field $\vec B$ are separated by which force?
questions.explanation: The magnetic part of the Lorentz force drives positive and negative charges to opposite ends, creating an emf.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: A loop enters a region of increasing magnetic field into the page. To oppose the change, the induced current's own magnetic field points:
questions.explanation: To oppose the increasing into-page flux, the induced current creates a field out of the page.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: The negative sign in Faraday's law $\mathcal{E} = -\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt}$ expresses:
choices: (c) Lenz's law: induced emf opposes flux changes
questions.answer: (c) Lenz's law: induced emf opposes flux changes
questions.explanation: It encodes that induced currents resist the change that produces them.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: Eddy currents are:
choices: (b) Loops of induced current in bulk conductors
questions.answer: (b) Loops of induced current in bulk conductors
questions.explanation: Changing magnetic fields induce circulating currents that cause heating and magnetic braking.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: Which situation will NOT induce an emf in a conducting loop?
choices: (a) Changing the magnetic field through the loop
(b) Changing the loop's area in a magnetic field
(c) Rotating the loop in a magnetic field
(d) Keeping field, area, and orientation all constant
questions.answer: (d) Keeping field, area, and orientation all constant
questions.explanation: With constant magnetic flux, Faraday's law gives zero induced emf.

resources.type: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2 – 13.1 Faraday’s Law

questions.question: A transformer operates primarily due to:
questions.explanation: A changing magnetic flux in the core induces emfs in primary and secondary windings.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation: One weber is one tesla-square-meter of magnetic flux.

questions.question: In an RL circuit, the time constant $\tau$ is:
questions.explanation: For an RL circuit $\tau = L/R$, setting the rate at which current approaches steady state.

questions.question: Immediately after an RL circuit is connected to a DC source, the ideal inductor:
choices: (b) Opposes any change in current, acting like an open circuit
questions.answer: (b) Opposes any change in current, acting like an open circuit
questions.explanation: Inductors resist sudden changes in current, so the initial current is limited.

questions.question: Self-inductance is:

(b) Induction only between two distinct coils
questions.answer: (a) Induction of emf in a coil by its own changing current
questions.explanation: A changing current alters its own flux and so induces an emf in the same circuit.
